top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P003) remains my first choice on distinctiveness of voice, formal achievement and sustained quality. Public knowledge of her work (Eros the Bittersweet, Plainwater, Autobiography of Red, Nox, Decreation, Antigonick, Norma Jeane Baker of Troy) suggests a recurring method that spans decades: she reopens classical and later texts to ask how inherited forms carry present grief and desire, and she does so in a dry, exact voice that turns suddenly exposed. I would rest the citation on her verbal, lyric and narrative achievement and give less weight to the book-object works, which text and translation carry poorly. I would also leave translation out of the credited scope. This case is less firmly demonstrated than the others. My knowledge of the breadth of her oeuvre is public and unverified, and her reception is concentrated in Anglophone culture. The open late-work tests for Cărtărescu and Adonis are no more resolved, so they do not make her case weaker. Cărtărescu (P002) is my second choice, because his large, unmistakable prose architecture is the strongest competing case, though I still have not seen whether his late volumes keep their emotional and moral range. Adonis (P001) is third, since a language-level renewal is a serious and durable kind of achievement, but I cannot assess the Arabic prosody and the supplied record does not settle whether his later decades deepen the project. P000 is last: translation limits apply to every candidate and do not justify withholding the prize.
